title: Understanding the flow behavior around Krueger flaps through the means of CFD simulations
abstractText: Abstract This study aims to establish the feasibility of Krueger flaps acting as high lift devices on a natural laminar wing aircraft configuration. It is part of the German funded project ‘ULTIMATE’, aiming an aircraft wing design providing fuel savings up to 10% as compared to aircrafts today at the next short to medium range aircraft expected to enter the market in 2030. The current paper aims to outline the status of implementing Krueger flaps as leading edge high-lift system, arranged in distributed manner and the ability to achieve handling quality requirements in high-lift configuration, and taking into consideration failure cases, which allows compact kinematic and system designs fitting into the restricted space of the aerodynamic profile. The current work focuses on the evaluation of the achieved low-speed performance by Computational Fluid Dynamics as well as first insights into critical failure cases with Krueger flaps jammed in unfavorable positions.

title: Divergent Diagrams of Folds Associated with Reflections
abstractText: Abstract We analyze divergent diagrams of k -fold map-germs at $$(\mathbb {C}^n,0)$$ ( C n , 0 ) , for $$k, n \ge 2,$$ k , n ≥ 2 , associated with reflections, adapting to the complex setting the theory of folds associated with involutions at $$(\mathbb {R}^n,0)$$ ( R n , 0 ) . In the complex case, a k -fold is naturally related to a cyclic group generated by a reflection, which guides the analytic classification of singularities. Under the conditions of transversality and linearity of the associated reflections, certain conditions related to the nontrivial eigenvalues appear as invariants by simultaneous conjugacy. We also provide a complete classification of pairs of transversal linear reflections and the corresponding divergent diagrams.

title: Terahertz electrodynamics and kinetic inductance of disordered titanium–vanadium alloy thin films
abstractText: Disordered superconductors represent an important area in modern condensed matter physics, where superconductivity survives even in the presence of strong electron scattering and localization effects. Understanding how disorder modifies the high-frequency electrodynamic response is not only important from a physics point of view but also essential for developing next-generation quantum detectors and superconducting devices. In this work, we investigate the terahertz electrodynamics of disordered Ti40V60 alloy thin films using terahertz time-domain spectroscopy to understand the relationship between disorder, quasiparticle dynamics, and kinetic inductance. By analyzing the complex conductivity, penetration depth, and superfluid response, we observe variations in the inductive response under different deposition conditions. Unlike conventional nitride superconductors that require tightly controlled reactive growth conditions, Ti40V60 alloys provide a simpler and more adaptable route for investigating the superconducting parameters under different deposition conditions. These findings demonstrate the THz electrodynamic response of the Ti40V60 alloy thin films and highlight their potential for kinetic inductance detector applications.

title: Representation learning in diffusion and flow-based model: an application aspect
abstractText: Abstract Diffusion models and flow-based models have recently become the dominant paradigms in generative modeling, largely due to their ability to learn rich, multi-level visual representations through large-scale training. This creates a bidirectional relationship between generative models and representation learning: improving representation learning enhances generation quality, while the learned representations can be leveraged for broader understanding tasks. This survey systematically explores this interplay with a focus on applications. We propose a three-tier progressive framework that organizes existing works from three perspectives: using representation learning to improve generative capabilities, exploiting generative models to extract representations for perception tasks, and ultimately moving toward general-purpose unified applications. We systematically categorize representative methods across a wide range of downstream tasks, including image classification, dense visual prediction, instance-level perception, and annotation-scarce scenarios. By providing a unified taxonomy and identifying key challenges, this survey aims to clarify the underlying logic of current research and suggest promising directions for future exploration. We hope this work can serve as a valuable reference for researchers interested in harnessing the representation power of generative models for applications beyond generation.

title: A simplified Fazekas scale for efficient assessment of white matter hyperintensities
abstractText: Background White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are key neuroimaging markers of cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD) and are associated with neuropsychiatric symptoms in older adults. Although the Fazekas visual rating scale is widely used in research, its clinical adoption remains limited. Therefore, we developed a simplified Fazekas visual rating scale (sFazekas) for overall WMH assessment to facilitate clinical application. Methods We randomly selected 900 participants from three MRI scanners and evaluated the reliability and scoring efficiency of sFazekas versus the Fazekas scale. Then, all participants were grouped according to the sFazekas scores, and intergroup differences among the different scores were analyzed. Next, we examined correlations among the sFazekas, the Fazekas, and WMH volume. Finally, we explored associations between the sFazekas and vascular risk factors related to CSVD. Results The sFazekas demonstrated excellent inter-rater reliability ( κ = 0.851) and required significantly less time to complete than the conventional Fazekas ( p < 0.01). Significant differences in age, WMH volume, and vascular risk factors were observed across sFazekas score groups ( p < 0.01). The sFazekas scores were strongly correlated with Fazekas scores for both deep and periventricular white matter, as well as with WMH volume ( p < 0.001). Ordinal logistic regression indicated that age, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and a history of stroke were independent predictors of higher sFazekas scores ( p < 0.001). Conclusion The simplified Fazekas visual rating scale (sFazekas) demonstrates reliability comparable to the conventional Fazekas scale, with the practical advantage of shorter scoring time, suggesting its potential utility in the clinical assessment of overall white matter hyperintensity burden in patients with cerebral small vessel disease.

title: AcWRKY22 activates AcMYB210 to regulate light induced anthocyanin accumulation in kiwifruit leaves
abstractText: Background Plant leaves often develop red coloration in response to aging and environmental changes. High light or continuous light treatments can elevate anthocyanins, which we observed in normally green kiwifruit leaves. Methods and results The underlying mechanism in this response was investigated using transcriptomic analysis. Results revealed that multiple anthocyanin biosynthesis genes, particularly Flavonoid-3-O-glucosyltransferase ( AcF3GT1a ), ( AcF3GT4 ) can convert unstable anthocyanidins into stable colored anthocyanins, and glutathione-S-transferase ( AcGST1 ) is responsible for the safe delivery of anthocyanins from the endoplasmic reticulum to the vacuole, were significantly upregulated under continuous light light-stress treatments. AcMYB210 , a member of the S6 MYB subfamily in kiwifruit with previously unknown function, was specifically induced. Dual-luciferase, yeast one-hybrid, and homologous genetic transformation assays confirmed that AcMYB210 directly binds to and activates the promoters of anthocyanin pathway genes, thereby promoting anthocyanin accumulation in kiwifruit leaves. A light-induced transcription factor, AcWRKY22 , was found to directly bind and activate the AcMYB210 promoter. In addition, AcMYB210 was highly expressed in plants whose leaves turned red after waterlogging stress. Conclusions In summary, our data reveal the critical role of the AcWRKY22-AcMYB210 module in mediating light signal regulation of anthocyanin biosynthesis in kiwifruit leaves, providing new insights into the regulation of kiwifruit anthocyanin biosynthesis by light signals.

title: The effect of transformational leadership on nurses’ turnover intention: the mediating effects of person-organization fit and career calling
abstractText: Aims This study aims to explore the relationship between transformational leadership, person-organization fit, career calling, and turnover intention among nurses. Additionally, it investigates whether person-organization fit and career calling serve as independent and chain mediators in the link between transformational leadership and turnover intention. Methods The researchers selected a convenience sample of 1,342 nurses from four Grade A-III hospitals in Shandong Province between October and November 2025. They collected data using several instruments: the General Population Questionnaire, the Transformational Leadership Questionnaire, the Person-Organization Fit Scale, the Career Calling Scale, and the Intent to Leave Scale. Descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and regression analysis were conducted using SPSS 26.0. To examine the chained mediation effect, they applied Model 6 in PROCESS 3.5 and estimated the 95% confidence interval using the Bootstrap method with 5,000 repeated samples. Results The results demonstrated that transformational leadership had a positive correlation with both person-organization fit and career calling, and a negative correlation with turnover intention. Mediation analysis revealed that over half of the protective effect of leadership on turnover intention was indirect, mediated through three pathways: person-organization fit alone, career calling alone, and their sequential chain. All indirect effects were statistically significant. Conclusion These findings show that transformational leadership reduces turnover intention through various complementary psychological mechanisms. This highlights the importance of relational fit and intrinsic motivation in understanding leadership effectiveness. The sequential mediation pathway reveals how organizational and personal factors interact to influence nurses’ career decisions, offering a more nuanced theoretical framework for retention research.

title: Analisis Deteksi Manipulasi Gambar Menggunakan Error Level Analysis dan Deep Learning di SD Padedewatu
abstractText: Digital images are increasingly used as documentation in educational environments, while image-editing tools make manipulation increasingly accessible. This study analyzes a workflow that combines Error Level Analysis (ELA) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for preliminary detection of manipulated images using photographs from SD Padedewatu as a case study. The dataset initially consisted of 34 original photographs. Because the supplied photographs did not contain verified manipulation labels, controlled manipulated variants were generated from each source image using copy-move, splicing, and object-erasure operations. The resulting labeled dataset contained 136 images, consisting of 34 authentic and 102 manipulated images. ELA was applied by recompressing each image and visualizing the resulting compression-error differences. A CNN classifier was then trained on ELA representations. To reduce source-image leakage, 24 source-image groups were used for training and 10 source-image groups were reserved for testing, producing 96 training images and 40 testing images. The model achieved 75% test Accuracy, 75% precision, 100% recall, and an F1-score of 85.71%. However, the confusion matrix showed that all test images were predicted as manipulated, including the 10 authentic images. Therefore, the Accuracy value should not be interpreted as evidence of balanced or robust forgery detection. The experiment provides a reproducible local ELA-CNN workflow and identifies dataset balance, sample size, and external validation as important priorities for subsequent research.

title: Disseminated BCG disease and recurrent pulmonary infections in a child with trisomy 21 carrying a novel BACH2 variant of uncertain significance: a 5-year case report
abstractText: Background Trisomy 21 is associated with combined immune dysregulation, including lymphopenia, impaired responses to vaccines, and heightened susceptibility to respiratory infections, driven in part by triplication of chromosome 21-encoded interferon receptor genes. BACH2 haploinsufficiency is a rare monogenic immunodeficiency characterized by lymphopenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, and susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases. Co-occurrence of these two conditions has not been previously described. Case presentation We report a 5-year longitudinal course in a Kenyan girl with trisomy 21, congenital heart disease, aspiration, and severe gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) found via whole exome sequencing to carry a heterozygous BACH2 missense variant (c.1420C > G;p.Leu474Val) of uncertain significance; parental segregation remains incomplete. In silico protein structural modeling (FoldX and Missense3D) yielded discordant predictions of the variant's effect on the protein’s stability and structure. Additional in silico pathogenicity predictions were also inconsistent: Sorting Intolerant from Tolerant (SIFT), Evolutionary Model of Variant Effect (EVE), PolyPhen-2, and CADD Phred scores predicted pathogenicity, while REVEL and AlphaMissense suggested a lack of deleteriousness. Persistent panlymphopenia and profoundly low IgM levels were documented throughout the follow-up period. Over these 5 years, the girl sustained six hospitalized lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs), with four requiring intensive care, which were disseminated Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) disease, respiratory syncytial virus and SARS-CoV-2 infections, and influenza A(H1N1)pdm09 pneumonia. Chest computed tomography at 4 years showed bilateral consolidations without bronchiectasis. Annual autoimmune screening remained negative. Conclusion This case illustrates the burden caused by severe and diverse respiratory pathogenic infections in a child with trisomy 21 and a candidate BACH2 variant. Trisomy 21 alone plausibly explains much of the phenotype; an independent contribution from the BACH2 variant remains unproven pending functional and segregation studies. Clinical considerations supported by this case include the potential value of prevaccination immunological screening to prevent BCG disease, equitable access to viral prophylaxis, and early specialist engagement in refractory cases.

The effects of realistic mathematics education and direct instruction on students’ mathematical critical thinking abilities: Considering levels of mathematical resilience
abstractText: Indonesian elementary school students’ mathematical critical thinking abilities (MCTA) remain suboptimal, highlighting the need for more effective instructional approaches. However, limited evidence has compared the effectiveness of Realistic Mathematics Education (RME) and Direct Instruction (DI) while considering students’ mathematical resilience (MR). This study aimed to examine the effects of RME and DI on students’ MCTA while considering their MR levels. A quantitative quasi-experimental design was employed with 34 fifth-grade students from an elementary school in Padalarang Village, Indonesia. The intervention consisted of three 70-minute instructional sessions. Data were collected using an MCTA test and an MR questionnaire and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Students in both groups showed significant improvements in MCTA. Although the RME group achieved slightly higher MCTA acquisition than the DI group, the difference was not statistically significant. However, RME produced significantly greater MCTA improvement than DI. Students with different MR levels showed significant differences in both MCTA acquisition and improvement, and MR had a significant positive effect on MCTA. No significant interaction effect was found between the learning approach (RME and DI) and MR. Overall, both RME and DI effectively improved students’ MCTA, with RME yielding greater improvement regardless of students’ MR levels.

Hybrid 99mTc-DTPA Dynamic Scintigraphy and SPECT/CT Overturn Presumed Renal Agenesis by Characterizing a Functioning Pelvic Ectopic Kidney in Pediatric VACTERL Association: An Observational Analytic Study
abstractText: Background: Renal anomalies occur in over 60% of children with VACTERL association, and ultrasonography often misses pelvic ectopia, leading to false diagnoses of renal agenesis. Distinguishing agenesis from functional ectopia is important before major spinal surgery. Objective: To characterize differential renal function and anatomical location in a child with suspected VACTERL association and sonographically presumed renal agenesis, using hybrid 99mTc-DTPA dynamic scintigraphy and SPECT/CT. Methods: A 4-year-old girl with thoracic hemivertebra, secundum atrial septal defect, thoracolumbar scoliosis (Cobb angle 32°) and a non-visualized left kidney on screening ultrasound underwent dynamic planar 99mTc-DTPA scintigraphy (74 MBq) followed by low-dose hybrid SPECT/CT at Dr. Hasan Sadikin General Hospital, Bandung, Indonesia. Differential renal function (DRF), Gates glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and renographic drainage kinetics were evaluated. Results: Planar scintigraphy overturned the diagnosis of renal agenesis by showing functioning tissue in both kidneys (DRF 34.6% left vs 65.4% right; net counts 5,873 vs 11,092 cpm). Gates GFR was 21.2 mL/min for the left and 40.0 mL/min for the right kidney (global 61.2 mL/min; 209.8 mL/min/1.73 m² normalized to body surface area). The left renogram showed delayed transit (Tmax 17.0 vs 11.0 min; retention index 0.897 vs 0.577). SPECT/CT localized the functioning left kidney to the pre-sacral pelvis, anterior to S1–S3, supporting a posterior-only approach to spinal instrumentation. Conclusion: Hybrid 99mTc-DTPA scintigraphy and SPECT/CT distinguished a functioning pelvic ectopic kidney from presumed renal agenesis, quantified 34.6% viable renal function and reduced the risk of intraoperative vascular injury during spinal deformity correction.

title: MOI LIEN QUAN GIUA ALBUMIN VA HOMOCYSTEIN HUYET THANH VOI HOI CHUNG LO LOC SHRUNKEN (SPS)
abstractText: Đặt vấn đề: Mức lọc cầu thận ước tính dựa trên creatinine có thể bị sai lệch bởi các yếu tố ngoài thận. Cystatin C cung cấp phương pháp ít bị nhiễu hơn. Thuật ngữ “Shrunken Pore Syndrome (SPS)” đặc trưng bởi sự giảm lọc chọn lọc các phân tử có kích thước trung bình và có liên quan mạnh đến tử vong tim mạch. Nghiên cứu này nhằm xác định các yếu tố sinh hoá có liên quan đến sự chênh lệch giữa hai phương pháp ước tính eGFR trong hội chứng lỗ lọc Shrunken tại Việt Nam. Phương pháp: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang trên 233 bệnh nhân bệnh thận mạn tại Khoa Khám bệnh, Bệnh viện Đại học Y Dược TP.HCM cơ sở 2. Bốn mô hình hồi quy được sử dụng để phân tích các biến số: chênh lệch mức lọc (diffcreacys = eGFRcrea - eGFRcysC), khác biệt eGFR (khi |diffcreacys| >= 15), tỷ lệ mức lọc (eGFRcysC/eGFRcrea), và tình trạng SPS (định nghĩa là eGFRcysC/eGFRcrea < 0,7). Các biến độc lập bao gồm giới tính, tuổi, albumin huyết thanh, homocysteine, LDL-C, HbA1c và BMI. Dữ liệu được xử lý bằng phần mềm Stata. Kết quả: Nữ giới có tỷ lệ eGFRcysC/eGFRcrea thấp hơn đáng kể so với nam giới ( = -0,103, p < 0,001). Tuổi cao làm tăng nguy cơ co lại của lỗ lọc (β = -0,0026, p < 0,05). Nồng độ albumin huyết thanh cao liên quan đến việc tăng tỷ lệ eGFRcysC/eGFRcrea (β = 0,138, p < 0,001) và giảm diffcreacys (β = 5,51, p = 0,001). Homocysteine có liên quan đến chênh lệch mức lọc diffcreacys (OR = 0,92, p < 0,05), trong khi LDL-C cho thấy mối liên quan yếu với tỷ lệ mức lọc (= 0,0006, p < 0,05). Kết luận: Sự khác biệt giữa hai phương pháp ước tính eGFR có thể phản ánh tình trạng bệnh lý tại màng lọc hơn là sai số tính toán đơn thuần. Nữ giới và người cao tuổi là những nhóm đối tượng nhạy cảm với SPS. Albumin và homocysteine huyết thanh có thể đóng vai trò là yếu tố liên quan đến sự hiện diện của hội chứng lỗ lọc Shrunken. SPS có thể giải thích rủi ro tim mạch tăng cao thông qua sự tích tụ các protein thúc đẩy xơ vữa. Do đó, cả hai chỉ số eGFR cần được đánh giá đồng thời trên nhóm bệnh nhân nữ và người cao tuổi để tránh bỏ sót các nguy cơ tim mạch tiềm ẩn.

title: Measurement distance effects on linear Taylor distributions for asymmetric radiation patterns with deep and filled nulls
abstractText: Abstract This study investigated measurement distance effects on asymmetric linear Taylor radiation patterns, including configurations with deep and filled nulls. An extension of the Elliott–Stern method was used to compute the complex roots required for independent side lobe and null control. The variation of illumination efficiency and radiation pattern error with measurement distance was analyzed and compared with those of symmetric Taylor distributions. The results showed that asymmetric side lobe depression provides higher illumination efficiency than symmetric counterparts while requiring comparable distances to achieve far-field behavior. The impact of null filling was also examined, demonstrating the existence of multiple admissible solutions that enable controlled trade-offs between illumination efficiency, dynamic range ratio, and far-field convergence distance.

abstractText: The development of culinary Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia has led to increasingly intense competition, particularly among ready-to-eat food businesses such as dimsum. This condition requires business owners to implement appropriate development strategies to increase their sales turnover. Dimsum Ratu Tulungagung is one of the culinary MSMEs facing several challenges, including fluctuating sales turnover, intense competition from similar businesses, limited human resources, and inadequate digital marketing. This study aims to formulate an appropriate business development strategy to increase the sales turnover of Dimsum Ratu Tulungagung based on SWOT analysis, as well as to describe the internal factor score (IFAS) and external factor score (EFAS). This research employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive research design. The research data consisted of the internal and external business conditions and the business development strategies implemented by Dimsum Ratu Tulungagung. The data sources included the business owner, operational employees, product display staff, regular customers, general customers, competitors in the dimsum business, and competitors from other culinary businesses. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation. The data were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing using SWOT analysis based on the Internal Factors Analysis Summary (IFAS) and External Factors Analysis Summary (EFAS) matrices. The findings indicate that the business development strategy of Dimsum Ratu Tulungagung to increase its sales turnover is positioned in the aggressive (SO) strategy quadrant, which emphasizes utilizing internal strengths to capitalize on external opportunities. The strategies implemented include strengthening brand identity, improving product quality and customer service, optimizing digital marketing, developing product innovations, and expanding market reach through participation in bazaars. These strategies contribute to a more relevant, competitive, and sustainable business development model for Dimsum Ratu Tulungagung.

title: Anesthetic management for pulsed field ablation in a patient with Eisenmenger syndrome using general anesthesia with spontaneous ventilation: a case report
abstractText: Abstract Background Drug-refractory atrial tachyarrhythmia is an important precipitating factor for recurrent heart failure decompensation in patients with Eisenmenger syndrome (ES). Although percutaneous pulsed field ablation (PFA) represents a potential therapeutic option for arrhythmia management, its application in this population is challenging due to the substantial anesthetic risks associated with severe pulmonary hypertension, right ventricular dysfunction, and profound hypoxemia. Case presentation We report the case of a 48-year-old male with ES and chronic heart failure who presented with recurrent, drug-refractory atrial flutter/fibrillation. Given concerns regarding hemodynamic deterioration during positive pressure ventilation, general anesthesia with spontaneous ventilation supported by a laryngeal mask airway was selected. The PFA was successfully completed without intraoperative hemodynamic instability. The patient was transferred to the ward with supplemental oxygen support. However, despite successful arrhythmia ablation and favorable intraprocedural physiology, he developed progressive heart failure and multiorgan dysfunction and died 20 days after the procedure. Conclusion The safe implementation of PFA relies on absolute immobility and stable hemodynamics. An anesthesia strategy utilizing general anesthesia with a laryngeal mask airway and spontaneous ventilation avoids the deleterious effects of positive intrathoracic pressure on right ventricular preload, allowing the PFA procedure to be completed with stable physiology and acute rhythm control.

title: Characterization of SPP1 + macrophages and their correlation with resistance to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in colorectal cancer liver metastasis
abstractText: Abstract Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) for colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major clinical challenge, with outcomes varying widely among patients, yet the mechanisms that drive therapeutic resistance remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated single‑cell RNA‑sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of patient tumor specimens to dissect the interplay between the hepatic tumor microenvironment and chemotherapy resistance. We identified a specific macrophage subpopulation marked by elevated expression of Secreted Phosphoprotein 1 ( SPP1 ) that is significantly enriched in insufficient responders to NAC. Mechanistically, these SPP1 + macrophages exhibit a pro‑tumoral transcriptomic profile and directly suppress CD8 + T cell cytotoxic function through the SPP1‑CD44 signaling axis, as demonstrated by in vitro co‑culture assays, a large‑scale tissue microarray, and multiple syngeneic mouse models. Spatially, they are scattered throughout the tumour and form dense barriers that sequester CD8 + T cells and drive their exhaustion. Strikingly, this spatial configuration inversely correlates with cytotoxic activity and adaptive immune signatures and thereby reinforces a local immunosuppressive niche that sustains chemoresistance. These data provide the missing link: effective chemotherapy requires an immune‑active hepatic microenvironment, and SPP1 + macrophage infiltration actively disrupts this state, which in turn promotes clinical resistance. In a preclinical CRLM model, SPP1 blockade synergised with anti‑PD‑1, inducing significant tumour regression and restoring T‑cell function. Collectively, our findings position SPP1 + macrophages as central drivers of NAC resistance in CRLM and highlight the spatial immune barrier they create as a promising therapeutic target for overcoming chemoresistance and improving immunotherapy responses.

A primary care-oriented framework for osteoporosis prediction: integrating multi-algorithm feature selection and machine learning model benchmarking
abstractText: Summary Large-scale screening and primary care diagnosis of osteoporosis are challenging due to the limited availability of dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Therefore, predictive models for osteoporosis that do not rely on bone mineral density measurements are essential. Using routine health examination data and applying a consensus feature selection strategy, we constructed machine learning (ML)-based models and compared their performance across multiple dimensions. Purpose To develop a robust, low-cost, and interpretable framework for osteoporosis prediction based on readily available information, which can be easily integrated into electronic health systems to inform DXA referral in resource-limited settings. Methods Variables covered by the basic health examination package were obtained from participants who underwent health examinations between January 2024 and January 2025. We implemented a strategy in which only features selected by at least four out of the seven feature selection methods were retained. Six ML algorithms were employed to develop models, and their prediction performances were compared across discrimination, goodness-of-fit, and clinical utility. Results A total of 2,260 participants were included, with an osteoporosis prevalence of 7.1%. Eight features: age, sex, body mass index, alkaline phosphatase, hematocrit, high-density lipoprotein, urea, and platelet count, were selected for model development. In the validation set, the random forest and artificial neural network (ANN) models demonstrated strongest screening performance, with AUCs of 0.895 (95% CI 0.867–0.923) and 0.890 (95% CI 0.862–0.919), respectively. The ANN model additionally exhibited superior calibration. Shapley additive explanations were applied to interpret the ANN model for osteoporosis prediction. Conclusion This study presents an easily integrable model for osteoporosis prediction based on routine health examination data. The ANN model provides robust prediction, offering a potential tool for pre-DXA triage and early identification of high-risk individuals in primary care and resource-limited settings.

abstractText: ABSTRACT Character education needs to be integrated into learning so that positive values are not merely understood conceptually but also practiced in students’ behavior. This study aims to describe the integration of character education among fourth-grade students in Arts, Culture, and Crafts (SBdP) learning at SD Negeri 90 Palembang. The study employed a descriptive qualitative approach, with participants selected through purposive sampling. The research informants consisted of the fourth-grade homeroom teacher, the Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PJOK) teacher, the Islamic Religious Education (PAI) teacher, and 26 fourth-grade students. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation, then analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings indicate that character education was integrated through habituation, role modeling, motivation, and the use of varied teaching methods. The eight character values identified were religiosity, discipline, hard work, creativity, independence, patriotism, social care, and responsibility. Religiosity, discipline, patriotism, and social care were well developed, while hard work and independence still required teacher guidance and reinforcement. The study concludes that SBdP learning can provide a setting for practicing character education through learning activities that allow students to create, interact, and demonstrate positive behavior. title: Association of childhood meat consumption with late-life cognitive function: mediation by adult education and moderation by parental literacy
abstractText: Background Results on the associations of childhood nutrition with late-life cognitive function are inconsistent, and little is known about whether family educational resources modify this association or whether adult education lies on the life-course pathway. We examined the associations of childhood meat consumption (CMC), used as an indicator of childhood nutrition, with late-life cognitive function and mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Moreover, we further examined whether these associations varied by sex, age, parental literacy, and socioeconomic status, and whether they were mediated by adult education. Methods Guangzhou Biobank Cohort Study (GBCS) participants, who were 50 years old and above with Guangzhou household registration and recruited from 2006 to 2008 were included. CMC was reported as never/about once a year, about once a month, about once a week, or almost daily. Cognitive function was assessed using the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), its four domains, and the Delayed 10-Word Recall Test (DWRT). Information on parental literacy and adult education was also collected. Multivariate linear, logistic regression and mediation analyses were done. Results In 8,865 participants aged ≥50 years, after adjustment for sex, age, and parental literacy, compared with participants who ate meat never or about once a year during childhood, those who ate meat about once a month, once a week and almost daily had higher MMSE scores [β (95% CI ): 0.33 (0.17–0.49), 0.83 (0.68–0.99) and 1.13 (0.93–1.32)] and lower odds of MCI [ OR (95% CI ): 0.84 (0.71–1.00), 0.55 (0.45–0.66) and 0.31 (0.22–0.42)], respectively. Associations were strongest for orientation. Frequent CMC (≥1/week) was more strongly associated with MMSE score [β (95% CI ): 0.73 (0.63–0.84)] among participants with literate parents and lower odds of MCI [ OR (95% CI ): 0.45 (0.38–0.54)] than among those with illiterate parents. Adult education mediated 40% [95% CI : 34.1%−47.3%] of the association between CMC and MMSE. Consistent results were found using DWRT. Conclusion More frequent CMC was associated with better late-life cognitive function and lower MCI prevalence, particularly among participants with literate parents. Adult education accounted for a substantial proportion of the association. These results provide new evidence that improving early-life nutrition and promoting educational attainment during early and mid-life may contribute to delaying and preventing cognitive impairment in later adulthood.

title: Development of Osmotic and Osmo-dried Asparagus racemosus Substitute using Maltitol and Applications of Linear Programming for Product Planning
abstractText: This study aimed to develop osmotic and osmo-dried Asparagus racemosus (Shatavari) using maltitol as a sucrose substitute and to optimize production planning through linear programming (LP). Shatavari samples were subjected to osmotic dehydration using sucrose or maltitol solutions at varying concentrations, followed by drying to produce osmo-dried products. Physicochemical properties, water activity, and sensory characteristics were evaluated to determine product quality and consumer acceptance. Results showed that substitution with maltitol yielded products with desirable sensory attributes comparable to those obtained with sucrose, particularly in osmo-dried samples, which demonstrated higher scores for color, texture, and overall acceptability, with overall liking scores ranging from 5.4 to 6.3 on a 7-point hedonic scale, indicating moderate to high consumer acceptance. The osmo-dried product exhibited lower water activity (0.65±0.021), which may contribute to improved microbial stability by inhibiting the growth of most bacteria and yeasts, although some molds may still grow under favorable conditions. Production optimization using the LP graphical method indicated that the maximum profit 385.35 THB could be achieved by producing 1.08 kg of osmo-dried Shatavari. A mixed production of 1.01 kg osmotic and 0.20 kg osmo-dried Shatavari yielded a profit of 293.23 THB. The integration of osmotic dehydration technology with sugar alcohol substitution and mathematical optimization demonstrates a promising approach for developing value-added, health-oriented products. These findings highlight the potential of Asparagus racemosus as a functional ingredient and underscore the relevance of LP modeling for small-scale food production and resource-efficient process design.

Stress reduces loss aversion without increasing reward-cue attentional salience
abstractText: Abstract Attentional and evaluative decision biases both shape motivated behavior, yet their interplay under acute stress remains unclear. We tested whether acute psychosocial stress affects loss aversion and reward-cue attentional salience. Sixty-one healthy adults completed the Montreal Imaging Stress Task (stress vs. control, between-subjects design), a mixed-gambling task to estimate loss aversion (λ) while conditioning cue-outcome associations, and a visual search task probing attentional salience of the conditioned cues, with concurrent autonomic and endocrine recording. Participants in the stress condition showed reduced loss aversion, attenuating the typical overweighting of losses relative to gains. By contrast, reward-associated cues reliably biased visual search, but this attentional capture did not differ by condition. Manipulation checks indicated heterogeneous physiological reactivity, which limits strong inferences about the null attentional effect. Overall, the findings are consistent with stress-related changes in evaluative weighting emerging more readily than changes in cue-driven attention under the present protocol. They further suggest that reductions in loss aversion do not necessarily require a measurable increase in reward-cue salience. Implications for understanding stress-related risky behaviors and the persistence of maladaptive cue-driven responses are discussed.

title: Safety awareness, attitudes, and behaviors among university students in Saudi Arabia: implications for pre-employment safety readiness
abstractText: Background Safety culture supports safe learning environments and is widely regarded as a determinant of safety practice, yet evidence among university students in Saudi Arabia remains limited. Because students represent the future workforce in safety-sensitive fields such as healthcare, engineering, and science, characterizing their safety awareness, attitudes, and behaviors is relevant to occupational health practice. This study assessed these three domains among students at a single private university in Riyadh and identified demographic factors associated with them. Methods A single-center cross-sectional survey was conducted among a convenience sample of 370 undergraduate and graduate students at Alfaisal University, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, using a previously validated 19-item questionnaire assessing safety awareness and attitudes (12 items) and safety behaviors (7 items). Descriptive statistics and multivariable generalized linear model (GLM) analyses identified demographic factors independently associated with each domain. Findings are discussed in relation to pre-employment safety readiness; workplace safety behavior and performance were not measured. Results Most participants were aged 18–22 years (76.2%), female (62.2%), and undergraduate (86.2%). Mean scores were 3.44 ± 0.71 for safety awareness and attitudes and 3.63 ± 0.69 for safety behavior. Female students scored significantly higher than male students on both safety awareness and attitudes ( β = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.12 to 0.42; p = 0.0006) and safety behavior ( β = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.08 to 0.38; p = 0.002). Non-Saudi students scored significantly higher than Saudi students on both safety awareness and attitudes ( β = 0.27, 95% CI: 0.10 to 0.44; p = 0.001) and safety behavior ( β = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.03 to 0.36; p = 0.010). Adjusted models accounted for a small proportion of variance (R 2 = 0.082 and 0.070, respectively). Age, academic level, marital status, and college affiliation were not significantly associated with either outcome. Conclusions University students showed generally positive yet moderate safety awareness, attitudes, and behaviors. Gender and nationality were the only variables that reached statistical significance in the adjusted models, and the associated effects were small. Because subsequent workplace safety readiness and performance were not measured, these findings describe students at one point in time and do not demonstrate future occupational behavior. They identify pre-workforce groups with lower current scores and provide baseline, hypothesis-generating evidence for multicenter and longitudinal studies in Saudi Arabia.

title: Design of a novel hybrid advanced adiabatic compressed air and gravity energy storage system
abstractText: Abstract To enhance the energy efficiency and energy density of physical energy storage (PES) systems, this study introduces a novel hybrid advanced adiabatic compressed air and gravity energy storage (HAACAGES) system. This system integrates advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) and gravity energy storage (GES) components, utilizing the mass of the compressed air (denoted by Δ m ) to make the HAACAGES system overwhelm the capabilities of individual systems. A numerical analysis model was established to validate the proposed system. Results demonstrate the HAACAGES system outperforms the individual systems in terms of both energy efficiency and density. Specifically, the energy efficiency is always higher than the sum of the individual systems at altitudes from 0 to 3 km. At 3 km altitude, the energy density reaches nearly 1.5 times that of conventional AA-CAES systems. At 1 km altitude, it exceeds 10 times that of conventional GES systems. Overall, the HAACAGES system shows clear potential as a promising solution for the next generation of large-scale PES systems.

abstractText: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengetahui dan menganalisis pengaruh likuiditas, aktivitas, dan leverage terhadap nilai pasar yang diproksikan dengan Earnings per Share (EPS). Likuiditas diproksikan dengan Current Ratio (CR), aktivitas diproksikan dengan Fixed Asset Turnover (FAT), sedangkan leverage diproksikan dengan Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR). Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan jenis data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan perusahaan yang mengalami boikot dan terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI). Teknik pengambilan sampel menggunakan metode purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, sehingga diperoleh 6 perusahaan sebagai sampel selama periode 2018–2024. Metode analisis data yang digunakan adalah analisis regresi linier berganda dengan bantuan program Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) versi 20. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa likuiditas yang diproksikan dengan Current Ratio (CR) tidak berpengaruh terhadap Earnings per Share (EPS). Aktivitas yang diproksikan dengan Fixed Asset Turnover (FAT) berpengaruh terhadap Earnings per Share (EPS). Sementara itu, leverage yang diproksikan dengan Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR) juga berpengaruh terhadap Earnings per Share (EPS).

title: Effectiveness of Silver Diamine Fluoride on Streptococcus mutans and Lactobacillus: A Systematic Review
abstractText: Objective: This systematic review evaluated the efficacy of silver diamine fluoride (SDF) at various concentrations, follow-up intervals, and in combination with other agents in reducing Streptococcus mutans (S. mutans) and Lactobacillus, as well as comparing its effectiveness with other antimicrobial agents.Material and Methods: A systematic search was conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, PubMed, and Google Scholar for studies published up to 31 December 2023. Eligible studies included both in vitro and clinical studies evaluating the effects of SDF on S. mutans and Lactobacillus. Extracted data included SDF concentration, follow-up interval, and antibacterial outcomes. The risk of bias was assessed using the appropriate tools, according to the study design. Results: Twenty-four studies met the inclusion criteria. In vitro studies consistently demonstrated the strong antibacterial effects of SDF, with increased efficacy at higher concentrations. Clinical studies reported significant reductions in S. mutans and Lactobacillus for up to six months post-treatment. When compared to other agents, SDF showed comparable or superior antibacterial efficacy. Most studies showed a moderate to high risk of bias. Conclusion: SDF demonstrated significant antibacterial activity against S. mutans and Lactobacillus in both laboratory and clinical studies. Its efficacy is influenced by factors such as concentration, follow-up interval, and combination with other agents. Despite methodological variability limiting the certainty of evidence, the current findings support SDF as an effective antibacterial agent against cariogenic bacteria. Further well-designed and standardised clinical trials with longer follow-up periods are needed to strengthen the evidence base and validate its comparative effectiveness in caries management.

title: Next-Generation Embedded Systems: Advanced Design Methodologies, Real-World Applications, and Emerging Technology Trends
abstractText: The evolution of embedded systems is more rapid and is bringing about a transformation across all systems of healthcare, automotive, industrial automation, and consumer electronics where intelligent, energy efficient and application specific solutions are becoming more important. The paper seeks to describe the complete analysis of next generation embedded systems especially in designing new approaches, practical implementations of the systems, and technological trends. The paper uses a structured review methodology; it would therefore pull together results of recently published peer-reviewed sources, industry reports, and case studies. Analysed methodologies are hw/sw co-design, power/energy conscious architecture, AI-driven optimisations, security-aware design and model-based development processes. The review findings also underscore the fact that a combination of edge AI accelerators, heterogeneous computing systems and secure, reconfigurable systems both maximizes performance per-watt and operational resiliency. The analysis also shows that new enablers like 5G/6G connectivity, neuromorphic computing and quantum-inspired algorithms will redefine embedded capabilities in application areas that generate particular latency and mission-critical applications. The discussion explains some of the major issues that the dialogue addresses such as security weaknesses, interoperability gaps, and sustainable design prerequisites. Every conclusion re-iterates the need to focus future research on cross-disciplinary research to come up with more scalable, secure, and eco-friendly embedded systems. The synthesis provides guidance to academic researchers, engineers and practitioners in the industry to utilize the current state of art developments in embedded systems, into the real world.

title: In vitro assay and GC-MS profiling of Proteus sp.EKWG2I3 isolate obtained from Echinops kebericho M.: a traditional medicinal plant
abstractText: Abstract Endophytic bacteria are a promising source of bioactive compounds valuable to medicine, agriculture, and industrial applications. This study investigates bioactive compounds of EKWG2I3 to evaluate their in vitro antibacterial and antioxidant activity against test strains. A healthy root of Echinops kebericho M. medicinal plant was collected for experimental analysis. 16 S rRNA gene sequencing was performed for accurate identification of a single potential isolate. In vitro antibacterial, antioxidant activities, and Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS) profiling of crude extracts for EKWG2I3 isolate were performed. The potent isolate ( EKWG2I3) obtained from E. kebericho M. clustered with P. mirabilis ATCC 29,906 T (ACLE01000013) and designated as Proteus sp. EKWG2I3 (PV635194). The results revealed that the crude extract of the Proteus sp.EKWG2I3 showed notable antibacterial activity of (15 ± 0.0529 mm) against E. coli ATCC-25,922 T . This isolate also exhibited potent free radical scavenging potential with an inhibitory concentration at 50% (IC 50 ) with value of 45.46 µg/mL compared to ascorbic acid. Moreover, GC-MS analysis identified methyl phenylacetate (38.49%) and pentanoic acid, methyl ester (12.71%) as major compounds in the extract of Proteus sp.EKWG2I3. This study suggests that Proteus sp.EKWG2I3 (PV635194) associated E. kebericho M.M. could be a potential source of bioactive compounds to combat emerging diseases caused by drug-resistant pathogens.

title: Inverse design of multi-mode OAM-generating pixelated THz metasurfaces
abstractText: Introduction Traditional metasurface design relies on physical priors and parameter scanning, which is time-consuming and prone to getting stuck in local optima. Methods In this article, we proposed a pixelated metasurface inverse design method, which discretizes the metasurface elements into a 16 × 16 binary pixel array, with each pixel independently adjustable, expanding the design space. We constructed a deep neural network framework consisting of a forward prediction residual convolutional network and a tandem generative inverse network: The forward network takes the element structure image as input and quickly predicts its complex reflection coefficient spectrum. Results and Discussion The average mean square error (MSE) of the test set is 0.0017. The inverse network is implemented by concatenating pre-trained forward networks without the need for real geometric labels, with an average MSE of 0.0131 on the test set. Using the trained model, we designed a metasurface that generates orbital angular momentum (OAM) with topological charges of ±1 and ±2 in the 1.5-1.6 THz frequency range. The full wave simulation results confirm that the designed metasurface can achieve spatial separation and independent control of multi-topology OAM beams, and the far-field amplitude and phase distribution are consistent with theoretical expectations. This method significantly improves the design efficiency and control accuracy of multifunctional metasurfaces, providing a new approach for on-demand customization of terahertz wave devices.

title: Development and Nationwide Multicentre Evaluation of Guideline-Grounded Large Language Model Chatbots to Support Patient Self-Management and Education in Rheumatology
abstractText: Abstract Patients with rheumatic diseases have persistent information needs that are not fully addressed in routine care. We developed and evaluated guideline-grounded, large language model (LLM) chatbots to support patient self-management and education in rheumatology. Ten disease-specific chatbots based on German guidelines were co-developed and deployed through 13 rheumatology centres and six patient organisations. Chatbot users rated responses and completed a questionnaire. User questions, feedback, and response characteristics were analysed using category-based coding and a six-dimensional LLM-as-a-judge assessment, with LLM-based ratings compared with rheumatologist ratings in random subsets. Between September 2025 and January 2026, 6291 questions were recorded. Thirteen question categories were identified, most commonly disease-specific questions (50.2%), medication and monitoring (37.3%) and diagnostics (28.2%). The chatbots were unable to answer in 263 interactions (4.2%). Of 2671 responses rated by users, 2481 (92.9%) received a positive rating. Insufficient detail was the most common reason for negative ratings (125/190, 65.8%). Among 602 questionnaire respondents, 84.6% reported that the chatbot was easy to use, 84.1% that answers were easy to understand, and 80.2% that it was a useful addition to patient education. In the LLM-based evaluation, 95.3% of answers were rated as completely safe and 79.1% as completely correct. Guideline adherence was assessed separately, with 45.0% rated as fully adherent; agreement with physician assessment was weak. Guideline-grounded chatbots received predominantly positive user feedback in real-world use, while LLM-based evaluation suggested that most responses were safe and correct. User questions and feedback may help guide iterative improvements to source content and patient education materials. Further studies are needed to evaluate educational effectiveness and independently validate response quality and clinical safety.

title: Development and internal validation of a CatBoost–SHAP-guided nomogram for significant liver fibrosis in children with chronic hepatitis B
abstractText: Background Significant liver fibrosis can develop in children with chronic hepatitis B (CHB), yet liver biopsy is invasive and unsuitable for repeated assessment. We developed an interpretable, non-invasive prediction model for significant fibrosis in pediatric CHB and evaluated whether baseline risk stratification was associated with subsequent treatment outcomes. Methods This retrospective study included 232 children with CHB who underwent liver biopsy, with significant fibrosis defined as Scheuer stage S ≥ 2. Patients were randomly assigned to a development cohort (80%) and a held-out test set (20%). A CatBoost model with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization was used to identify the most informative predictors, and these variables were incorporated into a logistic regression nomogram guided by Shapley additive explanations (SHAP). Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis, and DeLong testing. Associations between baseline risk groups and longitudinal outcomes were examined using generalized estimating equations adjusted for age and sex and Kaplan–Meier analyses. Results Significant fibrosis was identified in 96 children (41.4%). Liver stiffness measurement, alanine aminotransferase, and platelet count were retained in the final model. The nomogram achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.828 (95% CI, 0.767–0.889) in the development cohort and 0.782 (95% CI, 0.637–0.927) in the held-out test cohort, with performance comparable to that of the CatBoost model ( P = 0.240). Compared with the low-risk group, high-risk patients showed greater longitudinal reductions in alanine and aspartate aminotransferase, whereas longitudinal changes in liver stiffness measurement and hepatitis B virus DNA were similar between groups. Conversely, low-risk patients achieved virological suppression, HBeAg seroconversion, and biochemical response earlier than those classified as high risk. Conclusions An interpretable three-variable prediction model based on CatBoost-guided feature selection accurately identified significant fibrosis in children with CHB while maintaining performance comparable to the machine-learning model. Baseline risk stratification was also associated with subsequent treatment outcomes, although external validation is needed before clinical implementation.

Strategic Enhancement of Technical and Non-Technical Competencies in Mechanical Engineering Vocational Education
abstractText: This study discusses strategies to strengthen technical and non-technical competencies in the Mechanical Engineering vocational education program (STTAL) to develop superior Indonesian Navy human resources (TNI AL) that can adapt to the dynamics of modern maritime operations. This study used a qualitative approach and a literature review method, examining accredited scientific journals, international articles, official TNI AL documents, the Strategic Plan (Renstra), and STTAL performance reports. The results indicate a technical competency gap in using Industry 4.0 technologies (such as VR, IoT, and intelligent machinery systems), as well as weaknesses in non-technical competencies such as adaptive leadership, teamwork, and soldier resilience. Through thematic analysis, this study found that integrating a hybrid teaching factory, using simulation and virtual reality, strengthening a competency-based curriculum, and fostering industry-military collaboration are key strategies for closing this gap. Furthermore, an adaptive organizational culture and a sustainable quality management system at STTAL are essential prerequisites for ensuring the strategy's implementation supports the vision of superior and professional TNI AL human resources. This study offers a conceptual model of an integrated competency-strengthening strategy that can serve as a reference for developing policies and reforming military vocational education within the TNI AL.

title: Fe-mediated phase evolution and defect regulation in flexible Cu2Se films for enhanced thermoelectric transport
abstractText: The monoclinic copper selenide (α-Cu2Se) is a promising thermoelectric (TE) material due to its ordered Cu sublattice and intrinsically low thermal conductivity for near-room-temperature applications. However, excessive Cu vacancies in α-Cu2Se lead to carrier overconcentration and limit TE performance, whereas the disordered Cu sublattice of β-Cu2Se provides a potential route for carrier transport regulation. In this work, flexible Fe-incorporated Cu2Se films were fabricated by combining low-temperature hydrothermal synthesis with screen printing and subsequent thermal annealing. Moderate Fe incorporation enables the controllable α/β phase evolution and defect landscape modulation, promoting structural reconstruction and optimizing Cu-related defect chemistry. Structural analysis is consistent with partial Fe occupation at Cu sites in β-Cu2Se, together with the formation of a crystalline Fe2O3 secondary phase. Such regulation exploits the complementary characteristics of ordered α-Cu2Se and defect-mediated β-Cu2Se, leading to a balanced carrier concentration and mobility relationship for enhanced thermoelectric transport. As a result, the optimized Fe-doped Cu2Se film exhibits a maximum power factor of 657 μW m−1 K−2 at room temperature. Furthermore, a flexible six-leg thermoelectric generator fabricated from the optimized film delivers an open-circuit voltage of ∼12 mV at ΔT = 40 K and a maximum power of 9.46 nW at ΔT = 29.1 K. This work provides insights into Fe-regulated α/β phase evolution and Cu-related defect engineering in flexible Cu2Se films, offering a promising strategy for developing near-room-temperature flexible thermoelectric generators.

title: Environmental concern as a mediator of sustainable purchase intention among urban consumers in India
abstractText: Abstract The growing emphasis on sustainable consumption and responsible production has increased scholarly interest in understanding consumers’ sustainable purchase intentions (SPI). This study is based on the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and Value–Belief–Norm (VBN) theory and aimed to explore the impact of Green Brand Perception (GBP), Eco-Friendly Packaging (EFP), Social Media Engagement (SME), and Perceived Consumer Effectiveness (PCE) on SPI, with the mediation of Environmental Concern (EC) as a construct. A structured questionnaire and purposive sampling technique were used to collect data from 392 urban consumers who are concerned about the environment among the metropolitan cities in India. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was used for the analysis of the proposed conceptual framework using the SmartPLS 4.0 software. To ensure methodological rigour, reliability and validity assessments, mmoodel fit, non-response and common method biases were performed. The results indicated that PCE is the best predictor of SPI, followed by EC, EFP, GBP and SME. Environmental Concern is a significant factor for the sustainable purchase intention but not significant between PCE and SPI. This study is a valuable addition to the sustainability marketing literature as it combines both TPB and VBN theory in an emerging-market environment and demonstrates the importance of psychological and Behavioural factors in influencing sustainable consumption. The study offers important implications for marketers, policymakers, and sustainability advocates in designing ESG-oriented communication strategies, environmentally responsible branding initiatives, and digital sustainability campaigns aimed at promoting sustainable consumer behaviour.

Differences in microbiota profiles of simple and complicated pediatric appendicitis cases
abstractText: This study aimed to identify the differences in microbial composition between simple appendicitis (SA) and complicated appendicitis (CA) in a limited sample size using culture and microbiota analysis. Appendix tissues and rectal swabs for microbiota analysis and conventional cultures were collected from patients. 16S rRNA regions were amplified using a DNA preparation kit with primers designed to target the V3-V4 region. Sixteen (41%) of the patients were classified as CA based on the histopathological analysis, and the rest as SA. The effect size was slightly greater in rectal swab samples than in appendiceal tissue samples. Based on the conventional culture, the most common aerobic bacteria were Escherichia , Klebsiella spp., and Enterococcus spp. A decrease in both Pseudomonadota and Bacteriodota phyla was observed in tissue samples, while a decrease in Bacteriodota and an increase in Pseudomonadota were observed in rectal samples. Differences in the relative abundance of Coprobacter and Hungatella were observed between CAT and SAT samples; however, no genus-level difference remained significant after ANCOM-BC2 multiple-testing correction. The most notable feature of the CAT group was the relatively higher presence of potential pathobionts. Bacteriodes and Roseburia showed higher relative abundance in the SA rectal (SAR) group. The genera Eubacterium and Clostridioides showed a significant increase in both the SAR and CA rectal (CAR) groups. Lower relative abundances of Parvimonas, Prevotella , and Dialister and a higher relative abundance of Tyzzerella were observed in CAR compared with controls, although these differences did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction. In the ANCOM-BC2 pairwise analysis, an unclassified genus within Enterobacteriaceae was significantly enriched in CAR compared with healthy controls (LFC = 3.56, q = 0.003). No statistically significant distinction was shown at the alpha and beta diversity levels between SA and CA cases. Our findings support previous studies on increased density and diversity at the phylum level in the CA group. The main limitations were the limited sample size and the use of pre-operative antibiotics. Microbiota profiling of appendiceal tissue and rectal swab samples may provide complementary information for understanding microbiota-associated patterns in appendicitis; however, the diagnostic or predictive utility of these microbial profiles requires validation in larger, independent cohorts using dedicated predictive modeling and diagnostic performance analyses.

title: Multiscale pH fluctuations on a stable algal reef community (SE Sardinia, Tyrrhenian Sea)
abstractText: The Mediterranean Sea is threatened by ocean acidification and warming, in combination with habitat loss, pollution, invasive species, and overexploitation. Assessing local high-frequency pH variability in the context of relevant basin-scale time series data is essential to understand ecosystem vulnerability. We report the results of the Italian national pH monitoring based on the Marine Strategy Framework Directive, and the pH dynamics observed at Capo Carbonara. An experimental station equipped with a pH sensor and CTD probe was deployed at 32 m depth on a sandy bottom bordered by Coralligenous assemblages. Physical and biogeochemical variables were continuously recorded over 345 days and analyzed through additive time series decomposition. The benthic assemblages were surveyed by photographic and destructive sampling in summer and autumn 2016 and spring 2017 on algal reef and sandy bottom, to describe the biological components undergoing and contributing to the pH fluctuations. Seasonal pH variability ranged up to 0.2 units annually and 0.1 units daily, with maxima in January and minima in August, while the range of pH on the basin scale had higher mean values and exceeded local variability. Assemblage changes were driven by algal turf development and the invasive Caulerpa cylindracea . Coralligenous taxa appear stable, despite the substantial natural pH variability, shaped by meteo-marine conditions, water mass circulation, Saharan dust inputs, and benthic biological processes, with primary producers and calcifiers exerting a key influence. The ongoing trend of increasing temperatures and decreasing pH may threaten the Coralligenous ability to cope with the shifting future boundaries of such variability.

title: Simple renal cysts are associated with ischemic stroke in young adults: a case–control study
abstractText: Background The incidence of ischemic stroke among young patients is increasing, and ischemic stroke has become a major cause of death and disability in young adults. The key to alleviating this problem is to identify the risk factors and causes of stroke to optimize treatment. The current study aims to assess whether simple renal cysts are associated with the occurrence of ischemic stroke among young adults. Methods Data from patients with acute ischemic stroke aged 18–50 years and age- and sex-matched controls who underwent medical examinations at the Affiliated Changsha Central Hospital, Hengyang Medical School, University of South China, from October 2022 to September 2025 were retrospectively collected. Potential risk factors (including blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, dyslipidemia, homocysteine, and simple renal cysts) were compared between young patients with stroke and controls. Binary logistic regression analysis was conducted to identify risk factors for ischemic stroke among young patients. Results A total of 219 young patients with acute ischemic stroke and 219 controls were enrolled for analysis. Patients with elevated blood pressure, elevated blood glucose, and concurrent simple renal cysts had a higher risk of ischemic stroke. Simple renal cysts were associated with a higher risk of ischemic stroke in young adults, but they did not correlate with greater stroke severity. Conclusion Simple renal cysts are associated with ischemic stroke in young adults and thus merit clinical awareness. Prospective multicenter cohort studies are expected to confirm this association and clarify potential mechanisms.

title: Ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: evidence from human peripheral blood and mouse brain
abstractText: Background Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) has high morbidity and mortality. Ferroptosis may contribute to aSAH-related brain injury, but its peripheral and brain-associated signatures remain unclear. Methods Human peripheral-blood dataset GSE36791 (43 aSAH, 18 controls) was analyzed using limma, FerrDb intersection, WGCNA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and PPI-based prioritization. qPCR validation was performed in peripheral blood from 10 aSAH patients and 10 non-SAH controls; aSAH samples were collected within 24 h after rupture. Mean ages were 60.2 ± 7.7 and 63.6 ± 8.9 years, with 5 and 4 males, respectively. Brain-level validation used GSE79416 mouse cortex and OMIX006611 mouse SAH single-cell RNA-seq data. Male C57BL/6 J mice (8 weeks, 20–22 g) underwent cisterna magna autologous blood injection; brain tissues were collected 1 day after SAH (n = 6/group). Immune infiltration and molecular docking were also performed. Results Among 2,645 DEGs, 35 were ferroptosis-related. MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD were prioritized as ferroptosis-associated candidate genes and were upregulated in human aSAH peripheral blood, mouse SAH cortex, and the clinical qPCR cohort. Single-cell analysis showed expression of the corresponding mouse genes across annotated brain cell types, especially immune/glial populations. In mouse SAH brain tissue, MAPK3/ERK1, STAT3, PGD, and G6PD protein levels increased, p-STAT3/STAT3 ratio was elevated, MDA content increased, and GPX4 activity decreased. Immune profiling showed increased neutrophils, mast cells, and activated dendritic cells. Ganoderic acid A was prioritized as a preliminary in silico candidate. Conclusion MAPK3, STAT3, G6PD, and PGD are ferroptosis-associated candidate genes in aSAH, supported by human peripheral-blood, mouse cortex, single-cell, and mouse brain validation. Ganoderic acid A remains an exploratory in silico candidate requiring further functional validation.

abstractText: Nghiên cứu đánh giá hiệu quả ban đầu của các giải pháp nâng cao năng lực đội ngũ bác sĩ, kỹ thuật viên gây mê hồi sức sản phụ khoa tại Bệnh viện Sản nhi Bắc Ninh số 2 và 7 Trung tâm Y tế huyện, thị xã thuộc tỉnh Bắc Ninh cũ. title: Measurement of trainee autonomy in robotic-assisted lung resections using objective performance indicators
abstractText: Abstract Trainee autonomy in robotic-assisted thoracic surgery is critical for growth but difficult to quantify. Robotic platforms can log intraoperative kinematic and event data that can be transformed into metrics known as objective performance indicators (OPIs). This study sought to use OPIs obtained during robotic-assisted anatomic lung resections to assess trainee console autonomy at a high-volume robotic center. OPI data were obtained from 59 lobectomies and segmentectomies performed on a multi-port robotic platform between March 2022 and May 2023. Cases were divided into anatomic steps and annotated by a team of verified video reviewers. Console autonomy was assessed based on average path length (PL) of controllers and active time (AT) on the trainee console as a ratio compared to the overall PL and AT of the operation. Cases included 51 (86%) lobectomies and 8 (13%) segmentectomies. Average overall PL ratio was 0.15 (SD 0.17) and overall AT ratio was 0.23 (SD 0.23) for senior trainees. Autonomy was highest for inferior pulmonary ligament division (PL ratio = 0.39, AT ratio = 0.42) while lowest with pulmonary artery dissection (PL ratio = 0.10, AT ratio = 0.14). There was a significant association between AT and PL ratio with estimated blood loss (PL p = 0.036, AT p = 0.047). AT and PL ratios can provide objective surrogates of autonomy in thoracic surgery and can be stratified by individual case components. OPIs will offer valuable metrics for surgical education and assessment as national accrediting bodies shift graduation requirements towards case component proficiency over volume.

title: SHAP-guided adaptive feature weighting for phishing URL detection with a federated learning extension
abstractText: Abstract Machine-learning phishing URL detectors routinely report accuracies above 97%, yet four weaknesses undermine these results: absent statistical testing, unfair latency benchmarking, uninterpretable predictions, and an inability to use data held privately across organisations. We address all four on the Hannousse-Yahiouche benchmark (11,430 URLs, 87 features). We introduce the SHAP-Guided Adaptive Feature Weighting (SAFW) layer, a trainable component initialised from XGBoost SHAP scores and evaluate seven architectures (including a DistilBERT reference case) with 10-fold cross-validation, twenty-one McNemar tests, five class-imbalance ratios, and CPU-only latency benchmarking. XGBoost dominates centralised training (97.00% accuracy, 0.79 ms latency); no statistically detectable difference was observed between SVM and BiLSTM (McNemar p = 0.469). Extending to a twenty-client federated setting (matching the N ≥ 20 convention in the federated-learning literature) under non-IID Dirichlet partitioning with a per-client sample guard, federated SAFW-Hybrid reaches 95.4% ± 0.5% over the final rounds on the same 80/20 split, showing no statistically detectable difference from its centralised counterpart (95.45%; McNemar p = 0.30; paired-difference 95% CI [− 1.05, + 0.22] pp against a ± 0.5 pp margin not formally equivalent, as the CI is not wholly contained within the margin). A naive federated XGBoost ensemble loses 4.2 points, but a purpose-built horizontal federated GBDT (cyclic federated XGBoost) recovers almost all of this (94.5–95.1%), matching federated SAFW-Hybrid within test-set noise. Excluding the two externally-sourced features (google_index, page_rank) leaves centralised and federated accuracy largely intact (within ~ 1% point) but sharply reduces class-imbalance robustness, with F1 at the most extreme ratio variying by 35.6% points depending on architecture. Cross-client analysis shows google_index remains highly stable across the twenty simulated clients under the evaluated non-IID FedAvg setting (mean weight 0.891, spread 0.0013) under a non-saturating initialisation, ruling out sigmoid saturation as the cause; because the clients are coupled through repeated FedAvg aggregation rather than trained in isolation, this stability is reported as a property of the evaluated setting rather than independent cross-client convergence. XGBoost therefore remains the accuracy leader in the centralised setting; no statistically detectable difference was observed between XGBoost and SAFW-Hybrid under the evaluated federated setting once aggregation is done properly; the federated value of SAFW-Hybrid is competitive accuracy combined with an interpretable, cross-client-stable per-feature weight vector that a tree ensemble cannot provide.

title: Formation of LiFN2 with puckered LiF layers via nitrogen intercalation under high pressure
abstractText: The incorporation of molecular guests into ionic frameworks under pressure can produce host–guest structures inaccessible under ambient conditions. Here, we report the synthesis of an intercalated compound, LiFN2, at 105 GPa and 2100 K using the laser-heated diamond anvil cell technique. In situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, combined with first-principles calculations, reveal that nitrogen intercalation transforms the compact, three-dimensional B1 structure of LiF into a layered architecture. Puckered LiF layers extend parallel to the crystallographic ac plane, with individual LiF layers alternating with single layers of N2 molecules along the b axis. This structural transformation is accompanied by a change in electronic properties: whereas LiF is insulating, LiFN2 is predicted to be an indirect-gap semiconductor with a calculated bandgap of 3.7 eV. These findings demonstrate that a close-packed ionic framework can accommodate molecular guests through substantial structural reorganization under extreme conditions, providing insight into pressure-induced intercalation and the formation of layered host–guest compounds.

title: Exploring incontinence and toileting among children with additional needs
abstractText: Background The likelihood of a childhood additional need is elevated among high-risk infants and the likelihood of incontinence is elevated among children with additional needs. Although successful toilet training may reduce the prevalence of incontinence among children with additional needs who were identified as a high-risk infant, there is very little research regarding incontinence and toilet training among this group of children. Aims The aim of this study is to determine how many 5- and 6-year-old children with additional needs who previously participated in a service for high-risk infants experience incontinence, and to describe the caregiver experience of toilet training this group of children. Methods In this exploratory study, participating caregivers completed an online questionnaire which included quantitative and qualitative questions. Results Drawing from data provided by 17 caregivers, we found that 13 out of the 18 children we investigated experienced incontinence, and we identified five themes relating to the toilet training experience among caregivers: caregiver expertise, emotions, determining the leader, taking action, and evaluating progress. Conclusion In this exploratory study, we found the majority of 5- and 6-year-old children with additional needs who previously participated in a service for high-risk infants experienced incontinence. Our results also described the challenges caregivers experienced when toilet training this group of children. Findings from this study support further research into the barriers and facilitators of continence attainment for children with additional needs who were identified as a high-risk infant.

title: The rate of total hip arthroplasty after closed reduction of late-detected hip dislocation
abstractText: Aims The outcome of late-detected developmental dysplasia and dislocation of the hip (DDH) deteriorates with the length of follow-up. The aims of this study were to explore the rate of total hip arthroplasty (THA) with follow-up to patient age 60 to 76 years, and to define risk factors for THA. Methods Inclusion criteria were patient age at diagnosis < three years, closed reduction, and no acetabular procedures. A total of 114 patients (147 hips) met these criteria: 98 females and 16 males with a mean age of 1.4 years (0.4 to 2.7). Residual acetabular dysplasia was defined as centre-edge (CE) angle < 20° at skeletal maturity. Information on THA was obtained from the Norwegian Arthroplasty Register. Results Overall, 39% of the hips (n = 54) had residual dysplasia at skeletal maturity, with a mean CE angle of 14.9° (7° to 19°). In total, 52 hips (35%) had undergone THA at a mean patient age of 53.2 years (33 to 71). Risk factors for THA were residual acetabular dysplasia and severe degree of avascular necrosis. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, with THA as the endpoint, showed survival rates of 95% in hips without residual acetabular dysplasia at patient age 50 years and 76% at 70 years. In hips with residual dysplasia, the survival rate was 83% at age 50 years and 41% at 70 years. The estimated mean survival time was significantly lower in hips with residual dysplasia than in hips without dysplasia (62.6 years vs 71.4 years; p < 0.001). Conclusion The long-term outcome was very good in hips with no residual dysplasia at skeletal maturity. Only 24% of such hips had undergone THA at patient age 70 years. Dysplastic hips showed markedly worse outcomes, with a THA rate of 59% at 70 years. Routine concurrent pelvic osteotomy at the time of reduction in children < three years at diagnosis is hardly indicated. Cite this article: Bone Jt Open 2026;7(10):1261–1268.
